subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping that suppresses the current/default agent when another configured agent, role target, or quoted/later mention signal means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but changing it affects stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-loop handling for existing multi-agent guild setups.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and drop messages that target other configured agents or unrelated roles.

options.title: Split into narrower trackers
options.body: Keep this broad issue for coordination while related open items own strict mention/reply precedence, role-trigger policy, and slash-command targeting separately.

options.title: Document current default routing
options.body: Treat current default-owner routing plus optional ignoreOtherMentions and allowBots policies as the intended contract and close conflicting requests after documenting the tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and drop messages that target other configured agents or unrelated roles.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger appears most connected to the Discord preflight, route-resolution, and shared mention-policy history that would need the product contract decision.
